title: IP ownership and chain of title, including AI-generated code
status_rationale: The formation values file lists 'IP assigned to this LLC', 'IP licensed to this LLC' and 'IP explicitly excluded' as TODO. Echelon components are published under licenses naming a licensor, but which person or entity holds title was not established. AI agents produce material portions of repository work (Praxis provenance).
target_answer: Echelon Foundry, LLC holds title to all Echelon software through a recorded founder IP assignment and invention assignment agreements with every person and contractor who contributes. Pre-existing IP retained by any person is listed and licensed to the company perpetually and irrevocably. Contributions produced with AI tools are identified through provenance records; we rely on the human authorship, selection and arrangement in our works and on AI provider terms that assign outputs to us, and we acknowledge that purely machine-generated portions may not be copyrightable. No security interest encumbers the IP.
current_practice: Unknown; title holder of Echelon IP is not established.
intended_practice: Execute founder assignment at formation; adopt contributor assignment for all contributors.
provable: Praxis provenance records identify agent versus human contributions in repositories, which supports but does not establish chain of title.
customer_statement: IP ownership documentation is not yet complete. A founder IP assignment to Echelon Foundry, LLC and contributor assignment agreements are planned.
open_questions: US Copyright Office guidance on AI-generated works is not seeded as a source.

title: Echelon component licensing, including PolyForm Noncommercial terms
status_rationale: The Unbound capability assessment (unbound@9b38de47:requirements/convergence/2026-11-24-master/07-ECHELON-CAPABILITY-ASSESSMENT.md) records that every inspected Echelon system except the Registry (MIT), the Echelon Diagnostic Framework (MIT) and the Echelon theme (UNLICENSED) is licensed under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, and that commercial licensing is a launch blocker. CNV-GOV-009 forbids release-1 production dependencies under a noncommercial license without an executed commercial license plus escrow or a fork right. It also records version mismatches between tags, registry and vendored copies. The Secure Construction Standard separately says to prefer MIT for original public tooling, which conflicts with current practice.
target_answer: Customers receive a written commercial license from Echelon Foundry, LLC covering every Echelon component in their deployment (including Limen, Forma, Folio, Strata, Praxis-derived tooling), regardless of the public PolyForm Noncommercial license, with escrow release and a perpetual fork right for the customer's own use if Echelon ceases to support it. Each deployment carries an SBOM that names every Echelon component by tagged release and digest and the license under which the customer holds it; the release check fails if a PolyForm Noncommercial component lacks a commercial license record (CNV-GOV-009 AC-1). The licensor of record on public licenses is the LLC.
current_practice: Echelon components are publicly licensed under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. No commercial license has been executed or offered. Component versions are inconsistent across tags, registry and vendored copies.
intended_practice: Draft a commercial license and attach it to customer agreements; align public license licensor to the LLC; pin dependencies to tagged releases with digests.
provable: The public license files and the capability assessment establish the noncommercial licensing; nothing establishes commercial rights.
customer_statement: Most Echelon components are currently published under the PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 license. A commercial license covering customer production use is not yet available; we will not ask a customer to rely on the noncommercial license for production use.
residual_risks: Whether a nonprofit's own use qualifies as noncommercial under PolyForm terms is a legal question; relying on it for a vendor-operated service is unsafe.
open_questions: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 is not seeded as a source (needed: SRC id for the license text).
Should the Secure Construction Standard's preference for MIT be reconciled with the PolyForm Noncommercial licensing of the stack?

challenge.customer_intent: Certainty that the customer has lawful, durable rights to use everything in its deployment.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Customer's production use is outside the license, or rights end when the vendor relationship ends.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Conventional vendors license proprietary code under the MSA; Echelon's public noncommercial license is unusual and must be superseded explicitly.
challenge.legally_required: Copyright law requires a license for use beyond the public grant; no regulation addresses it.
challenge.contractually_required: Customers routinely require warranties of title and non-infringement.
challenge.historical_convention: Proprietary license in the MSA plus escrow.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Thin dependency boundaries allow replacement of a component (capability assessment fallback).
challenge.automatic_enforcement: SBOM license gate fails releases containing unlicensed PolyForm components.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Per-release SBOM with license field and gate result.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Commercial license plus fork right plus SBOM gate.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, by inspecting SBOMs and executed licenses.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely once a commercial license exists; unlikely before.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Licensor of record is not the contracting entity; versions in deployment differ from licensed versions.
challenge.alternative_risks: Customers may question why the public license is noncommercial and whether community contributions complicate title.
supporting_arguments: Source availability lets customers inspect what they run.
opposing_arguments: Procurement and legal teams may flag any noncommercial license in the supply chain as a blocker regardless of a side license.

title: Open source license compliance and SBOM license data
status_rationale: SEC-SUPPLY-001 (proposed) requires locked versions, provenance, SBOM, vulnerability and license checks. CNV-GOV-009 requires an SBOM license check. Neither is operating for a production Echelon service.
target_answer: Every release produces an SPDX or CycloneDX SBOM with license identifiers for all direct and transitive components. A license policy allowlist is enforced in CI: disallowed licenses (for example AGPL in network-served components, or noncommercial licenses without a commercial grant) fail the build, and unknown licenses fail until reviewed. Attribution notices are generated from the SBOM and shipped with the product.
current_practice: Not established for a production service.
intended_practice: Implement license gate in Praxis CI as part of SEC-SUPPLY-001.
customer_statement: Automated open source license checks and SBOMs with license data are planned and not yet operating.

title: Customer data ownership, permitted use and AI training rights
status_rationale: Business plan section 10.04 separates service use, retention, learning, evaluation, model training and publication rights as a draft position. Unbound requires third-party data rights and permitted AI use to be enforced in access, storage, retrieval and exports (SOC2-028) and a source registry with license and terms (UNB-EXT-017). Nothing is implemented, and the AI providers Echelon would use are not inventoried.
target_answer: Customers own their data and all outputs generated from it. Echelon uses customer data only to provide the service. Customer, donor, advisor and grantee data is never used to train, fine-tune or evaluate AI models, ours or a provider's, and is sent only to AI providers whose contract prohibits training on it and limits retention, verified per provider and per model endpoint. Aggregated or de-identified use for benchmarking requires the customer's opt-in. Purpose restrictions are enforced in the data access layer so that analytics or training pipelines cannot read tenant data without a recorded purpose grant. Third-party data license restrictions travel with the data into display, storage and export.
intended_practice: Contract terms plus purpose-bound data access in Unbound; AI provider inventory with training terms.
provable: Requirements and draft plan text only.
customer_statement: Echelon does not intend to use customer data to train AI models and plans to make that a contractual commitment enforced in the platform. These commitments are not yet contractually offered or implemented.

challenge.customer_intent: Donor and sponsor data is not used to benefit others or exposed through AI models.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Customer data appears in model outputs for other parties or is commercialized.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Contract clauses alone depend on the vendor's and AI provider's discipline and cannot be observed by the customer.
challenge.legally_required: Not directly, but privacy laws (GLBA, state privacy laws, CCPA service provider terms) restrict secondary use.
challenge.contractually_required: Increasingly common in enterprise and financial services contracts.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Tenant data reachable only through purpose-bound interfaces; no pipeline exists that exports tenant data to training.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Data access layer denies reads without a purpose grant; egress allowlist limits AI endpoints to approved no-training configurations.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Access logs with purpose, egress logs, provider configuration attestations.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Contract plus architectural purpose enforcement plus egress control.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Partially; customers rely on logs and assessments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Provider changes default retention or training terms; shadow use of AI tools by personnel.
challenge.alternative_risks: Purpose enforcement could hinder legitimate support work.
opposing_arguments: Customers cannot independently observe AI provider retention.

title: Source code access, escrow license scope and customer-specific deliverables
status_rationale: CNV-GOV-009 contemplates escrow or a fork right for noncommercial dependencies. No escrow, source license or deliverables policy exists.
target_answer: Customers receive a license that, on an escrow release event, permits them or a successor vendor acting for them to use, modify, host and maintain the software for their own operations, including all Echelon components. Customer-specific deliverables (integrations, configurations, migration scripts) are owned by or perpetually licensed to the customer; generic improvements remain Echelon's and are available to all customers.
intended_practice: Include in commercial license and escrow agreement.
customer_statement: Source license and escrow release terms are planned as part of the commercial license.

title: Third-party IP protection, trademarks and protection of customer confidential information
status_rationale: Business plan section 14.02 (confidentiality and generalized learning) and 14.03 (pre-existing and reusable IP) are drafts. AI coding tools are used in Echelon engineering; no code provenance or similarity scanning was located. No trademark registrations were reviewed.
target_answer: We prevent ingestion of third-party proprietary code or confidential information into our products: AI coding tools are used only under provider terms that include IP indemnity or duplicate-detection features where available, dependencies enter only through approved package sources (SEC-SUPPLY-001), and license and similarity scanning runs on releases. Customer confidential information is used only for that customer; generalized learning that a person retains is limited to methods and never includes the customer's confidential data or identifiable details. Product names are cleared before use and registered when commercially material.
intended_practice: Adopt AI tool usage policy and release scanning.
customer_statement: Controls against ingestion of third-party IP and a confidentiality policy covering generalized learning are planned. No IP claims history can be evidenced either way.
